subject: english-language
title: Descriptive & Narrative Writing Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the toolkit for vivid creative writing.
meta_desc: GCSE English Language descriptive and narrative writing walkthrough — imagery, senses, show don't tell.
final_note: You learned the core tools of descriptive and narrative writing — imagery, the senses, and showing not telling.

concepts.def: Opening hook, rising tension, climax, falling action, resolution; one event focus in short story.
Describe action and sensation rather than state emotion; 'tears welled' not 'she was sad'.
Five senses: sight, sound, smell, taste, touch; immerses reader; not just visual.
Realistic speech reveals character and advances plot; new line for new speaker; punctuation crucial.
Tone = writer's attitude; mood = reader's feeling; created by word choice, pace, imagery.
Satisfying ending: full circle, twist, ambiguity; avoid 'and it was all a dream'.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Don't write 'She was angry'. Write 'Her knuckles whitened around the mug'.

Telling is flat. Showing puts the reader inside the moment.

Strong description hits more than just sight. Sound, smell, touch and even taste pull readers in.

Example: 'The salty air stung my cracked lips; gulls screamed overhead.'

Use the weather to mirror mood. A storm before a fight. Sunshine on a reunion.

Example: 'The sky bruised purple as she opened the letter.'
